name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It sharpens fine details in complex scenes where other upscalers blur edges or lose texture, giving a measurable quality bump without extra compute cost. The trade-off is that depth-aware upscaling can over-smooth flat areas if the depth map is noisy, but EXCAVA’s current depth estimation is already robust enough to minimize that risk. RealVisXL’s face-preserving upscaler stays on hold until we confirm InstantX’s impact on non-facial regions.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—faces blur worse under motion because depth maps misread skin texture as noise. Test InstantX-ComfyUI on a 1080p face video: if LPIPS or FID scores don’t improve by 0.5% over RealVisXL’s waxy waxy faces, drop it. Otherwise, switch to a face-specific upscaler like GFPGAN 2.0—it trades speed for fidelity, but faces stay sharp.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL’s face-preserving upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline *only* on the face. It locks facial detail during motion where depth-aware upscaling fails, cutting blur that hurts viewer trust. The trade-off is higher latency—RealVisXL’s face model runs on CPU while the rest of EXCAVA stays GPU—but the 0.5%+ quality gain on the most critical element justifies it.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face model on CPU adds 1.2s per frame—too slow for real-time. Test it only if the face ROI is <20% of the frame; otherwise switch to a lightweight face enhancer like GFPGAN 2.0 running on GPU. Settle it with a 1080p face video: if GFPGAN 2.0’s FID improves by 0.5% over RealVisXL’s CPU version, adopt it—no latency tax.
